title: Informal Conjecture on similar growth of $N_{DFL}(\varepsilon)$ and $1/\delta_{TRL}(\varepsilon)$
statement_text: We suspect that $N_{DFL}(\varepsilon)$ and $1/\delta_{TRL}(\varepsilon)$ have similar growth.
context_text: The triangle removal lemma states that for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with fewer than $\delta n^3$ triangles can be made triangle-free by deleting at most $\epsilon n^2$ edges; $\delta_{TRL}(\epsilon)$ is the largest such $\delta$. The diamond-free lemma states that for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $N$ such that for every $n\ge N$, every $n$-vertex graph in which each edge lies in a unique triangle has at most $\epsilon n^2$ edges; $N_{DFL}(\epsilon)$ is the smallest such $N$. It follows from the triangle removal lemma, giving $N_{DFL}(\epsilon)\le1/\delta_{TRL}(\epsilon/3)$. For both quantities the best lower bound is of the form $(1/\epsilon)^{c\log(1/\epsilon)}$ (from Behrend's construction), while the best upper bound is $1/\delta_{TRL}(\epsilon)\le\mathrm{tower}(O(\log(1/\epsilon)))$ (Fox), a tower of $2$'s. The authors prove supporting evidence: for fixed $0<c<1$, if $N_{DFL}(\epsilon)\le2^{\epsilon^{-c+o(1)}}$ then $\delta_{TRL}(\epsilon)\ge2^{-\epsilon^{-c/(1-c)+o(1)}}$. Their motivation is the triangle-free lemma: for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $M$ such that every triangle-free graph $G$ has an $\epsilon$-approximate homomorphism (a map $V(G)\to V(F)$ sending all but at most $\epsilon|V(G)|^2$ edges to edges) to a triangle-free graph $F$ on at most $M$ vertices; with $M_{TFL}(\epsilon)$ the least such $M$, they show $M_{TFL}(\epsilon)\ge e^{\epsilon N_{DFL}(C\epsilon)/C}$, while $M_{TFL}(\epsilon)\le e^{O(\delta_{TRL}(\epsilon/C)^{-2})}$ is known; similar growth of $N_{DFL}$ and $1/\delta_{TRL}$ would thus give comparable bounds on $M_{TFL}$.
